episodes.157946: A thunderstorm produced a brief waterspout near Indian River Shores, while another thunderstorm produced a strong wind gust in southern Brevard County.
episodes.158150: Severe thunderstorms brought hail and damaging winds.
episodes.158317: Thunderstorms cause strong marine wind gusts as storms move across coast.
episodes.158771: Multiple marine thunderstorm wind gusts were observed as early to mid-evening thunderstorms and associated boundaries moved through the bays and coastal waters on June 14th and 15th.
episodes.158788: An unsettled weather pattern remained over South Florida with a mid-level trough  producing cool temperatures aloft and southwesterly flow keeping sufficient tropical moisture across the region. As sea breeze boundaries developed, the flow favored a dominant Gulf breeze, which helped to develop thunderstorms over the east coast metro areas. A few storms were strong enough to produce damaging winds.
episodes.158846: A surface front and drier air was settling southward across SE GA, with a differential heating boundary across NE FL near I-10 due to cirrus blow-off from storms in Appalachee Bay. Strong to severe storms formed across NE FL due to heating and interactions with the differential heating boundary and sea breezes.
episodes.158977: A number of severe thunderstorms developed across the area on the evening of June 15, resulting in many reports of tree damage, 1-inch hail, and building damage due to both winds and lightning strikes.
episodes.159059: Despite weak upper forcing and fairly strong convective inhibition (CINH) keeping the vast majority of South Central Nebraska storm-free on this early Tuesday evening, a pair of rogue, slow-moving supercell storms were able to breach the cap and produce hail to at least golf ball size in small portions of Buffalo and Clay counties. The far southeastern Buffalo County storm initiated first, shortly before 7 p.m. CDT, and drifted slowly south before rapidly dissipating only about an hour later. Along the way  though, it dumped hail up to 2 inches in diameter on Shelton. Just as this storm was fading the second one got going in southeastern Clay County around 8 p.m. CDT and followed a very similar life cycle, drifting slowly south-southeast and dissipating 60-90 minutes later, but not before dropping golf ball size hail north of Edgar that reportedly damaged crops and cracked vehicle windshields. A weaker storm that split eastward from the Clay County supercell briefly affected northwestern Thayer County, but once this convection died around 930 p.m. CDT with the onset of diurnal cooling, the remainder of the night was storm-free. ||This somewhat-surprising, albeit brief/localized event was a textbook case of why one can never say never to at least isolated robust convection in a high instability environment during summer peak heating. In the mid-upper levels, South Central Nebraska resided along the northeast periphery of an expansive ridge centered over the Four Corners region. Although deep-layer shear was respectable (around 40 knots), the flow over the Central Plains lacked any notable disturbances and fairly strong capping was present (as indicated by 700 millibar temperatures around 12 C). However, upon closer review, a subtle northwest-southwest oriented surface boundary was draped across the heart of the local area, promoting weak low-level convergence between light easterly breezes and light southerlies. This subtle convergence, in tandem with fairly robust mixed-layer CAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg (owing to temperatures/dewpoints well into the 90s/60s F) proved just sufficient enough to spark the isolated severe activity.
episodes.159311: A persistent upper-level trough over the eastern U.S. and a cold front dropping south through the state brought scattered strong and isolated severe thunderstorms to north and central Georgia.
episodes.159318: Isolated thunderstorms developed under a mid-level shortwave trough and along an outflow boundary. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.159686: The interaction of a cold front arriving from the west and a sea breeze circulation within a warm and moist environment led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.159687: The interaction of a cold front arriving from the west and a sea breeze circulation within a warm and moist environment led to severe thunderstorms that eventually shifted across coastal waters.
episodes.159688: The interaction of a cold front arriving from the west and a sea breeze circulation within a warm and moist environment led to severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
episodes.159838: As a cold front pushed into an environment of large MLCAPE (2000-3000 J/kg) and high DCAPE (1000 J/kg), scattered elevated thunderstorms developed on the nose of a 40 knot low-level jet across southwest Minnesota. These storms dropped south southeast through northwest Iowa during the evening producing periodic large hail and some damaging wind gusts as the low-level jet veered ahead of the advancing boundary.
episodes.160077: A very dry environment was in place on this day, with thunderstorm development expected to remain isolated. A few storms did develop along the I-25 corridor though, and produced high wind gusts as they moved across Pueblo county.
episodes.160627: A deep upper trough of low pressure extended down the eastern United States into the northeast Gulf of Mexico, with a deep cyclonic gyre in the Bay of Campeche.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developing over Cuba spread north and northeast, producing widespread gale-force wind gusts over the Florida Keys.
